# Shrink-only baseline: product repair literals that name a CLI flag or
# environment variable without a complete runnable tool invocation.
#
# Per ADR 0088 (docs/adr/0088-degraded-repair-actionability.md) and bd-9zfku:
# - `degraded[].repair` stays human-facing prose; advisory prose with no flag
#   and no command is explicitly valid and must never be handed a synthetic
#   command to satisfy this gate.
# - `degraded[].repairCommand` (`Option<String>`) carries the optional explicit
#   runnable command when one exists alongside human-facing prose.
# - A repair literal that names a CLI flag (`--<flag>`) or environment variable
#   (`EE_*`, `CARGO_*`, `RCH_*`, etc.) without a complete tool invocation in
#   either `repair` or `repair_command` is a defect class gated by
#   `scripts/check-degraded-repair-actionability.py`.
#
# THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. `scripts/check-degraded-repair-actionability.py`
# fails in both directions:
# - New arm: any flag/env-only repair site absent from this baseline (or whose
#   multiplicity exceeds the recorded count) fails.
# - Stale arm: any entry here whose site has acquired a runnable command (in
#   `repair` or `repair_command`) or been removed fails, instructing the author
#   to lower or delete the row.
#
# Format: <rel_path>\t<count>\t<normalized_repair_literal>
